# Copilot instructions

Guidance for AI agents working in this repository.

> **`CLAUDE.md` is the source of truth.** This file mirrors its non-negotiables for Copilot; if the two ever
> diverge, `CLAUDE.md` wins, and they must be kept in sync in the same change. The canonical depth lives in
> `docs/` (linked below).

## Project overview

FinTrack v2 is an AI-first personal finance manager. The primary interface is AI chat (Claude clients) talking to the backend's **MCP server**; REST is a secondary surface. Backend: TypeScript, Fastify, zod, libSQL (encrypted local SQLite via `@libsql/client`), Drizzle ORM, diplomat architecture, functional programming style. Full plan: `docs/PLAN.md`. v1 (NestJS/Mongo/React) is archived as functional reference only — never modify it.

## Development setup

```bash
npm install
npm run dev   # stdio MCP server by default (ADR-007), HTTP sidecar (REST /api + /ui dashboards) on by default too
```

The database is a local encrypted libSQL file (`fintrack.db`). On first run the encryption key is generated and stored in the OS keychain (`@napi-rs/keyring`). For CI/headless environments set `FINTRACK_DB_KEY` (64-char hex string) — never commit or log it. Containers should use `FINTRACK_DB_KEY_FILE` (absolute path to a file holding the key, e.g. a Docker secret at `/run/secrets/fintrack_db_key`) instead: resolution order is file → env var → keychain, setting both file and env is a config error, and with no source and no keychain startup fails fast (`openssl rand -hex 32`) — the key is never written next to the data. `HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`) sets the HTTP bind address. **Authentication (ADR-033, ADR-034):** `FINTRACK_AUTH` (`required`|`disabled`) defaults to `required` **everywhere**, a loopback install included (every route but `/api/health`, `/ui/login`, `/ui/setup` needs a session cookie or, on `/api`/`/mcp`, an access token); `disabled` is an explicit opt-out for development and tests (every request acts as the owner) and is a startup error on an exposed instance — a non-loopback `HOST`, or a reverse proxy named via `PUBLIC_URL`/`TRUST_PROXY`. So `npm run dev` needs a login too: claim the owner once with `npx tsx src/main.ts auth setup`, or run `FINTRACK_AUTH=disabled npm run dev` for loopback development. **stdio signs in too** (ADR-034 §2–4): `FINTRACK_TOKEN` (a personal access token in the client's env) → a saved keychain sign-in for `FINTRACK_PROFILE` (default `default`) → *not signed in*, where every tool call, resource read and prompt answers `FinTrack: not signed in. Open <origin>/ui/connect?code=ABCD-EFGH and confirm the code ABCD-EFGH.` until a person approves in the browser (`/ui/connect`), choosing scopes and a duration (this session only / 24 h / 7 d / 30 d); `npx @rafaelfcarneiro/fintrack@latest login` / `logout` do the same from a terminal, and an explicit `FINTRACK_AUTH=disabled` keeps stdio acting as the owner for development. **Always print and document `npx @rafaelfcarneiro/fintrack@latest …` (`NPX_COMMAND`, `models/package.ts`)** — unpinned `npx` prefers a stale installed copy — and an older build refuses to open a database a newer one migrated (the startup version guard). `PUBLIC_URL` (optional external origin, no path/trailing slash; `https` → `Secure` cookie, and the CSRF expected origin) and `TRUST_PROXY` (Fastify `trustProxy`, for rate limiting behind a proxy) complete the set; see `docs/auth.md`. With auth `required` a fresh instance prints a one-time **setup code** to stderr (`docker compose logs`) that `/ui/setup` exchanges for the owner's username and password — it claims the pre-existing owner row, never creates a user. The banner and `/ui/setup` also name the terminal route (`TERMINAL_SETUP_HINT`, `models/auth/message.ts`): `npx @rafaelfcarneiro/fintrack@latest setup <client>` — or `auth setup` alone — claims the same owner row from the terminal (username and password prompted without echo, or `--username` + `--password-stdin`; no TTY and no flag → exit non-zero before writing anything), and `auth reset-password [--user u]` sets a new password and ends that user's sessions, access tokens and approved sign-in requests in one batch (`src/diplomat/cli/commands.ts`, composed in `src/composition/cli.ts`; the CLI opens the database like the server but starts neither HTTP nor stdio). `users list | invite <u> [--admin] | reissue <u> | disable <u> | enable <u> | role <u> <member|admin>` manages who can sign in from the same trusted terminal (no password asked; `invite` and `reissue` print a one-time code and, only when `PUBLIC_URL` names the origin, a link (the CLI binds nothing, so it never guesses an address; otherwise it prints the page path) — the person chooses their own password at `/ui/access/invite`). `key export --to <file>` and `db export --to <file>` (the npm→Docker move, `docs/auth.md`) write the database key and a consistent encrypted snapshot (`VACUUM INTO`) to a new file: the key is never printed and never written beside the data (real paths compared), both files are `0600` (`wx`) and never overwritten, and neither command migrates the database.

The HTTP sidecar (REST `/api` + `/ui` dashboards) starts automatically alongside stdio — the dashboard experience is a core feature, not opt-in (ADR-013 Decision 7). Set `FINTRACK_HTTP=false` to disable it (stdio-only, no port bound). `MCP_TRANSPORT=http` switches the transport entirely instead (no stdio fallback; a bind failure there is fatal by design). `npm run dev` pins `PORT=3001` for either (package.json); the published package defaults to `PORT=51737` instead — deliberately not a common Node/Fastify dev-server port, to minimize collisions with other software (`docs/architecture.md` § HTTP sidecar). A bind failure for the sidecar (e.g. the port is already in use) is caught and non-fatal — stdio keeps working regardless; this is a resilience fallback, not the normal state.

- REST API: `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api` (from source) / `http://127.0.0.1:51737/api` (published package)
- MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP): `http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp` (from source) / `http://127.0.0.1:51737/mcp` (published package)
- Docker: `(umask 077; openssl rand -hex 32 > fintrack_db_key) && docker compose up --build` (on Linux also `sudo chown 1000 fintrack_db_key` first — the key file stays owner-only, never world-readable) serves everything on `http://127.0.0.1:51737` (ADR-032) — loopback publish only (plain HTTP); first start prints the setup code (`docker compose logs`) to claim the owner at `/ui/setup`; MCP clients and scripts connect to `/mcp` and `/api` with `Authorization: Bearer ftk_…`, a personal access token created at `/ui/access/tokens` (`docs/auth.md`, `docs/mcp-clients.md`); verify an image with `docker build -t fintrack:ci . && scripts/docker-smoke.sh fintrack:ci`.
- Run `npx ntl` for an interactive, described list of all scripts.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev             # tsx watch
npm run build           # tsc (tsconfig.build.json)
npm start               # node dist/main.js
npm run lint            # eslint (style/quality smell rules — part of the gate)
npm test                # vitest run (unit tests under test/unit)
npm run typecheck       # tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json (includes tests)
npm run test:integration # in-process libSQL DB, no Docker required
npm run test:all        # unit + integration
npm run mcp:inspect     # MCP Inspector — connect to http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp
```

Run a single test file: `npx vitest run --config vitest.unit.config.ts test/unit/logic/classify.test.ts`

Tests live under `test/unit/` and `test/integration/` (not colocated). The backend lives at the repo root (`src/`, `package.json`) — there is no `backend/` subfolder.

## Definition of Done (mandatory — verify before EVERY push, initial delivery and each PR-fix push alike)

Quality is delivered, not reviewed in. Before pushing any branch — first cut or a fix addressing review — you MUST run the self-review pass below, fix what it surfaces, and only then push. State the result of each item in the PR description (or the review reply for a fix). "I'll fix it if review catches it" is not acceptable; review is the backstop, not the gate.

**The gate (must be green on every push):**

```bash
npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:all && npm run build
```

**Self-review pass (do this every time, before the gate):** produce the diff (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`), read every changed hunk, and check it against:

1. **Read the source docs in full, not a summary — mandatory every time, not only for visibly "architectural" changes.** Open `docs/diplomatic-architecture.md`, `docs/functional-core-imperative-shell.md`, and `docs/code-quality.md` themselves before doing items 2-7 below. The condensed bullets elsewhere in this file (Architecture guidance, Agent-level non-negotiables, Documentation map) are a *pointer* to those docs, not a substitute for reading them — a change that only touches composition-root/entrypoint files (e.g. `main.ts`, anything under `src/composition/`) still counts as "architecture-related" and still requires this step. Skipping the real file and relying on a derived summary is how violations that are explicit in the source doc (e.g. cross-file literal duplication, covered below) get missed.
2. **Layering** (`docs/architecture.md` dependency table, `docs/diplomatic-architecture.md`, `docs/functional-core-imperative-shell.md`): `logic/` is pure (no I/O, no `diplomat`/`controllers` imports); the domain never imports seed (`diplomat/db/seed`); boundaries are zod-decoded; controllers return `ResultAsync` via `safeTry`; diplomats stay thin; composition-root wiring (e.g. code that imports from more than one `diplomat/*` submodule to wire them together) lives outside `diplomat/*`, not inside it. For a flow already converted under ADR-021 (`createAccount` so far), the controller returns `{ persist, response }` instead of writing — it must not call a repo write method or touch `Db`; only `diplomat/db`'s `runEffects` does.
3. **Constants over literals** (`docs/code-quality.md`): no bare string/number where a zod `.enum.*` or named constant exists, **and no literal — including log/error message strings, not just domain values — copy-pasted across two or more call sites, even across files.** If a value is used in more than one place, extract a shared constant/function; grep the diff for repeated substrings before calling this item done.
4. **Declarative over imperative** (`docs/code-quality.md` remeda table): no `xs.filter(...)[0]` → use `R.firstBy`/`R.find`; no manual accumulation loop → `R.groupBy`/`countBy`/`sumBy`/`mapValues`; no chained `.filter().map().sort()` → `R.pipe`. Native `map`/`filter` only for single-stage transforms. **Function shape** (`docs/code-quality.md` § Function shape): no switch of 7+ cases (lint) → an exhaustive `satisfies Record<Kind, …>` table; controllers read as gather → decide → persist; one named definition per MCP tool / HTTP route.
5. **Naming & single responsibility** (`docs/code-quality.md`): names don't restate their module; verb+noun; one job per function; file and folder names are kebab-case (enforced by lint (`eslint-plugin-check-file`) across `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/` and `ui/`).
6. **Tests are mandatory.** Any behavior change (`logic/`, `controllers/`, `adapters/`, `diplomat/db/repos/`, MCP tools) ships added/updated tests in the SAME change — success *and* expected-failure paths. A behavior diff with no test diff is incomplete. In the PR, list each behavior change → the test that covers it. (CI enforces this; don't rely on it — author the tests yourself.)
7. **Docs in the same change**: `docs/architecture.md` (structural changes), `docs/write-path.md` (write-path mechanics — the effect runner, appliers, outcomes, per-flow notes; update it, not `docs/architecture.md`'s § Write path summary, for anything below the always-loaded guardrails), `docs/mcp-tools.md` (tool changes), this file (data conventions), and the relevant `docs/designs/NNN` status line. When `CLAUDE.md`'s non-negotiables or Definition of Done change, mirror them into this file in the same change (`CLAUDE.md` is the source of truth; the two must not drift).

**Independent subagent verification (required for feature-sized changes).** The author is the worst reviewer of their own diff — it's easy to rationalize what you just wrote. For any feature-sized change, after your own self-review and a green gate, dispatch a fresh verification subagent (e.g. via Claude’s `Task` tool; if unavailable, request an independent review pass from another agent/reviewer) to re-audit the change independently, then fix what it finds before pushing. A change is "feature-sized" if ANY of these hold: it adds or changes an MCP tool; it touches the schema or a migration; it adds or revises an ADR or design doc; or its diff spans multiple layers or roughly five or more files. Small, single-file fixes need only the inline self-review above.

Give the subagent the diff and a verifier brief, not a vague ask. It should: confirm it read `docs/diplomatic-architecture.md`, `docs/functional-core-imperative-shell.md` (for write-path changes), and `docs/code-quality.md` directly (not a summary); read `git diff origin/main...HEAD`; check every hunk against all seven self-review items above and the dependency table in `docs/architecture.md`; confirm each behavior change has a matching test (success + expected-failure); confirm `docs/*` were updated in the same change; and return a concrete list of violations with file:line, not a "looks good". Treat its findings as a blocking checklist. It must also run two explicit checks, reporting each as pass/fail with evidence: (1) **engine boundary** — nothing in the diff re-implements what `@rfc0/effect-runner` owns (see the "Owned by" list under Layer rules): no retry/version-conflict handling, no bus or publish-isolation code, no copy of the persistence contract types; the only FinTrack code on the engine is port bindings (`diplomat/db`) and composition-root adapters such as `publishFor`; if the engine needs to change, the change belongs in the package first; (2) **imperative constructs** — in `src/logic/**`, `src/controllers/**` and `src/adapters/**` no `for`/`while`/`do` loops, no `let`, no `.push(` (the lint rule enforces it, and the verifier also checks for workarounds: `forEach` with mutation, `reduce` that mutates its accumulator, assignment through `Object.assign`/index writes on a collected array). Because it didn't write the code, it catches the constant-over-literal, remeda, and missing-test misses the author's eye skips.

Healthy design iteration (rethinking an approach mid-flight) is welcome and is NOT what this gate targets — it targets avoidable rework: style/remeda/constant misses and missing tests.

## Architecture guidance

Architecture and domain behavior are documented in canonical docs and should not be duplicated here.

Before changing architecture-related code, read:

- `docs/architecture.md` (as-built project architecture, invariants, dependency direction)
- `docs/diplomatic-architecture.md` (core Diplomat concepts) — **read the file itself**, not just the "Diplomat alignment in this project" summary in `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/functional-core-imperative-shell.md` (the core/shell split — the domain returns effects as data, the shell executes them; canonical/agnostic, mandatory alongside `docs/diplomatic-architecture.md` for any change that adds or touches a write flow)
- `docs/write-path.md` (the full as-built write-path mechanics — the effect runner, the applier catalogue, outcome/response shaping, per-flow notes; **mandatory before writing or changing any write-path code**. `docs/architecture.md` § Write path carries only the always-loaded guardrails and points here for the rest; project-specific, not canonical)
- `docs/code-style.md` (controller/logic/adapters implementation patterns)
- `docs/code-quality.md` (constants over literals, naming, single responsibility, no magic values) — same rule: read the file itself; this is reinforced as self-review item 1 above, not optional

"Architecture-related" includes composition-root/entrypoint changes (`main.ts`, anything under `src/composition/`), not only changes inside `diplomat/`, `controllers/`, or `logic/`.

Agent-level non-negotiables:

- **Diplomatic architecture is non-negotiable.** Follow the layer rules below exactly unless `docs/architecture.md` explicitly states otherwise for a specific case.
- **Constants over string literals.** Zod enums expose `.enum.*` — always use it. Never pass `'mcp'`, `'expense'`, or any other value that has a named constant. See `docs/code-quality.md`.
- **Declarative over imperative.** Prefer remeda (`countBy`, `groupBy`, `anyPass`, `allPass`, `pipe`, `conditional`, `mergeAll`, `firstBy`, …) over manual loops and mutation. See `docs/code-quality.md`.
- **Names don't repeat their module.** A function in `adapters/transactions.ts` is `modelToDb`, not `modelTransactionToDb` — the namespace at the call site provides context. See `docs/code-quality.md`.
- **Code quality principles apply to every line.** Read `docs/code-quality.md` before generating code. Violations will be caught in review.
- Keep `diplomat/*` thin (parse/delegate/translate) and put orchestration in controllers.
- **Edge vocabulary stays at the edge.** `models/`, `logic/` and `controllers/` never name an edge's vocabulary (tool names, routes, CLI commands): a domain error whose fix is another operation carries a `Remedy` (`models/remedy.ts`) and a neutral message; `diplomat/mcp` and `diplomat/http` each translate it into a `hint` (`remedy.ts`). `ToolName` lives in `diplomat/mcp/tool-name.ts` and is lint-restricted to the MCP edge.
- **Diplomat edge organization (ADR-025):** a new MCP tool/resource/prompt or HTTP route lives in the domain module matching its controller (`diplomat/mcp/tools/<domain>.ts`, `diplomat/http/routes/<domain>.ts`) — never inlined into `server.ts`/`routes.ts`, which stay thin aggregators. **One named definition per route/tool** (`const listAccountsRoute: RouteDefinition`, `const createAccountTool = defineTool(…)`); modules export lists; registration is generic (`diplomat/mcp/register.ts`'s `registerDefinitions`); tool names come from the `ToolName` enum (`diplomat/mcp/tool-name.ts`). A handler adapts args → model, runs the flow and maps the result in ~10 lines — longer is orchestration for a controller. All of `src/**` obeys the Function-shape lint limits (40 lines, complexity 10, depth 3, 15 statements) — a controller reads gather → decide → persist, the decide step a pure `logic/` plan function; in the shell a repo factory only binds a `RepoScope` and each query is a named function over it. See `docs/architecture.md` § Diplomat edge organization.
- **Read-side cross-aggregate correlation lives in controllers, not repos (ADR-028):** a repo queries only its own aggregate's table (including aggregations over its own dimensions); it never joins another aggregate's table to correlate or measure it — that's orchestration (controller) + a pure matching rule (`logic/`). A label-only `LEFT JOIN` (e.g. resolving a foreign key's display name) is not governed by this. See `docs/architecture.md` § Diplomat alignment in this project.
- Keep `logic/*` pure (no I/O or runtime state reads).
- Decode external boundaries with zod and keep expected failures on the Result track.
- If behavior changes, update `docs/architecture.md` in the same change.

Layer rules (enforce in review — violations are bugs):

- `logic/` never imports `diplomat/`, `controllers/`, or anything that does I/O.
- `diplomat/` contains no business logic — it parses, delegates, and translates.
- **The effect engine is the external package `@rfc0/effect-runner` (ADR-031)** — its behavior is documented in its own repo; FinTrack is a consumer and imports only its public API (semver range). `diplomat/db` is the SQLite adapter that implements its port. Engine changes are made in `RafaelFCarneiro/effect-runner`, released, then the dependency is bumped here.
- **Owned by `@rfc0/effect-runner` — never re-implemented here:** the effect runner (`runEffects`/`runEffectsSequence`, transaction-per-batch, ordering), retries and version conflicts (`VersionConflict`, `MAX_RUN_EFFECTS_ATTEMPTS`, transient-contention classification), the read-version check (`checkVersion`; FinTrack only implements the port's `check` in its appliers and calls the `persistence.check` builder — a read joins the conflict set by a check, never by rewriting the row), the persistence contract (`Persistable`, `PersistOutcome`, `FlowOutcome`, `INITIAL_VERSION`, `withPersistenceMeta`), and the change bus with its publish-failure isolation (`createChangeBus<E>`; FinTrack contributes only its `ChangeEvent` type and the `publishFor(userId)` adapter in `composition/runtime.ts`). Need something different from the engine? Change the package first, release it, then bump the dependency here — do not fork its behavior locally.
- **Imperative constructs are lint errors in `logic/`, `controllers/` and `adapters/`** (`eslint.config.js`): `for`/`for…of`/`for…in`/`while`/`do…while`, `let`, `.push(`. Use the remeda table in `docs/code-quality.md`, a pure helper, or recursion; `diplomat/**` and `composition/**` (the shell) may be imperative.
- Controllers return `ResultAsync<T, AppError>` (neverthrow) for **expected** failures (unknown account, ambiguous category…); unexpected errors throw and become 500s.
- Decode at the boundary: every external input (HTTP body, MCP args, SQL rows) is zod-parsed before entering the domain.
- Fastify routes: use `reply.send()` consistently — never mix with bare `return` in the same handler, as it causes hard-to-debug double-send issues.

## FP conventions (ADR-001, ADR-003)

This is a quick operational summary for agents. Canonical wording lives in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/code-style.md`.

One concern per library — don't cross them:

- **zod**: schemas + boundary decoding only.
- **neverthrow**: control flow for fallible operations. Controllers compose via `safeTry` generator pipelines — each `yield*` short-circuits on `err` (Railway-Oriented). Shared combinators: `guard`/`okOr` (`common/result.ts`), entity resolvers (`controllers/resolve.ts`). Controllers return `ResultAsync`; diplomats just `await` them.
- **remeda** ([docs](https://remedajs.com/docs/)): pure data reshaping in `logic/`/`adapters/` (`pipe`, `groupBy`, `sortBy`, `sumBy`, `countBy`, `firstBy`). Use when a transformation has ≥2 stages or needs grouping; native `map`/`filter` is fine for trivial cases.

## Data conventions

This is a quick operational summary for agents. Canonical wording lives in `docs/architecture.md`.

- IDs: `crypto.randomUUID()`; seeded nodes use stable English slugs (`cat-food`, `cat-transport`, …).
- Locale: the per-user `user_settings` table holds `locale` (`en|es|pt`) + `locale_source` (`default|inferred|explicit`) + `base_currency` (the `settings` singleton is instance-wide and empty today). Resolution: `FINTRACK_LOCALE` env → the caller's `user_settings.locale` → `'en'`. Default categories carry a JSON `names` column (`{"pt":"…","es":"…"}`); display names are resolved at read time as `names?.[locale] ?? name` (ADR-009). User categories keep literal names (`names = null`). Seeded translations are authored in `diplomat/db/seed/categories.ts`.
- Currency: BRL, USD, MXN, COP, USDC, and BTC seeded (ADR-026 Phase 1 — crypto is first-class alongside fiat, purely additive; MXN and COP are additive fiat, 2 decimals, Feature Design 022; no conversion or base-currency valuation implied by any of them, that's phases 2–3). Accounts/cards reference one currency (`currency` FK → `currencies`); transactions carry a denormalized `currency` column. `currencies.decimals` (fiat 2, USDC 6, BTC 8) drives display/rounding — `GET /api/currencies` and the `fintrack://currencies` MCP resource expose `{code, symbol, name, decimals}`. Summaries always group per currency — never convert implicitly; money-amount rounding in `logic/` uses each currency's own `decimals` (`roundToDecimals`/`decimalsLookup`, `logic/money.ts`), never a flat 2, so a native BTC/USDC amount isn't flattened to fiat precision.
- Amounts: full units (reais/dollars), positive numbers; `type` (`expense`/`income`) carries the sign.
- Dates: `YYYY-MM-DD` strings; month/year filters become date range conditions in SQL (`date >= from AND date < to`).
- Idempotency: every transaction write uses `UNIQUE(user_id, idempotency_key)` + `onConflictDoNothing()` (unique per user; the derivation names no user, so a statement imports for each user); `rowsAffected === 0` means duplicate — return existing row with `created: false`. The key is envelope metadata on the insert `Persistable` (`idempotencyKey?: string`, `Persistable` in `@rfc0/effect-runner`), never a `Transaction` domain-model field — a flow sets it alongside `model` when building the insert, and the applier writes it onto the fixed `idempotencyKey` column (never a per-registration name, ADR-029 Phase 2b), deduping on it. **The key is domain-derived, not caller-supplied** (ADR-029 Phase 2b): `logic/transaction.ts#deriveIdempotencyKey` hashes (sha256, over a `JSON.stringify`-serialized field array — never a plain string-joined concatenation, since the caller-supplied `discriminator` is otherwise-unconstrained text and a plain separator risks two different field combinations serializing to the same string) the write's full deterministic identity — funding source (account/card id), a transfer's destination account (`counterpartyId`, so two transfers sharing source/date/description/amount but different destinations don't collide), a card purchase's resolved bill cycle (`billPeriodKey`, `month-year` — an explicit `billMonth`/`billYear` override can target a different cycle than an otherwise-identical purchase), type, currency, date, normalized description, and the amount rounded via `roundToDecimals` (never a raw `.toFixed`, which truncates rather than rounds at a float boundary like `1.005`) to the currency's own decimals — plus an optional caller `discriminator` (`CreateTransactionSchema`/`CreateTransferSchema`), the escape hatch for a genuinely-distinct transaction that would otherwise derive an identical key. Single-add and bulk import share one derivation (bulk reuses the single-add flows per line, caching the currencies-list read once per batch the same way it already caches locale, rather than once per line). **One-time key-format discontinuity**: a statement re-imported after this landed won't dedup against pre-existing readable-format keys (possible duplicates of previously-imported rows) — accepted at personal scale, no backfill.
- Demo marker (Feature Design 022 §3, §5): `settings.instance_kind` (`standard|demo`, default `standard`) is the only source of "this is a demo" — not a file name, path or env var. `Tenancy.instanceKind`/`Deps.instance` read it (`diplomat/db/repos/instance.ts`); a demo database shows the banner and `[Demo]` titles on every HTML page (`diplomat/http/hooks/demo-marker.ts`), sends MCP `instructions` at initialize (`diplomat/mcp/instructions.ts`) and reports `demo: true` from `get_status`. Only the demo seeder (a later phase) writes `demo`.
- Classification: `classificationMethod` (`rule|history|user|none`) + `confidence` stored on every transaction; merchant knowledge lives in the `merchant_category` table (`merchant_key`, `category_id`, `weight`, `origin: rule|history`).
- MCP-created transactions store `rawInput` (original natural-language text).
- Credit cards: transactions reference a card (`credit_card_id`) and the cycle's bill (`bill_id`); the `bills` row (fatura) is auto-created `open` based on the card's `closingDay`. `pay_bill` only flips status — never creates a payment transaction (would double-count).
- Recurring: `recurring_rules` rows with `next_due`; materialized by `apply_due_recurring` with stable keys `rec-<ruleId>-<date>`.
- Bulk import: each item's idempotency key is derived by the same single-add flow the item dispatches to (`addAccountExpense`/`addAccountIncome`/`addCardPurchase`), against that item's own resolved account/card and currency decimals (fiat 2, USDC 6, BTC 8) — not a flat 2, so two crypto lines differing only past the 2nd decimal don't collide on the same key, including on an unattached (no-account) statement whose lines override `currency` per item. Items with confidence < 0.6 are flagged `needs_review`, not blocked.
- Transfers: transactions with `type: 'transfer'` and BOTH `from_account_id` AND `to_account_id` set (ADR-002) — one row for the whole movement. Summary/classification queries MUST exclude `t.type = 'transfer'`. Same-currency only until FX lands.
- Transaction status: `pending | effective`. `effective` = cleared, counts toward balances/summaries. `pending` = expected but not yet real; excluded from balances and summaries; confirmed via `confirm_transaction`. **Default is date-aware**: when `status` is omitted, future-dated transactions default to `pending`, past/present to `effective`; an explicit `status` always wins. Classification ignores status.
- Balances: derived, never stored — `initialBalance + income − expenses + transfers in − transfers out`. **Only `effective` transactions count.** Projection (effective + pending-through-date) is opt-in via `projectedAsOf` on `get_account_balances`.
- Tenancy (ADR-033 §5): every owned row (`accounts`, `credit_cards`, `bills`, `transactions`, `tags`, `budgets`, `recurring_rules`) carries `user_id NOT NULL`; the shared defaults (seeded categories, `rule` merchant edges, bundled `file` dashboards) carry `user_id NULL`, are read by everyone and changed by no one (`SHARED_DEFAULT_READ_ONLY_MESSAGE`). The edge builds `depsFor(principal)`/`runEffectsFor(principal)` per request (stateless, partial application): repos are `xRepo(db, userId)` (no method takes a user id; every owned-table query filters `user_id = :me`, shared-default tables `user_id = :me OR user_id IS NULL`), appliers are `xApplier(userId)` (insert stamps the user, update/delete add `AND user_id = :me`). A controller never sees an unscoped repo or runner; an edge handler without a principal fails closed. Another user's id or name is `unknown_*`, never forbidden. A new owned table needs `user_id`, a scoped repo, a scoped applier, a row in the isolation suite (`test/integration/tenancy/`), and a line in the `docs/architecture.md` tenancy map. The change bus carries `userId`; `/ui/events` forwards only the stream's own user's events.
- Identity: the owner plus invited users; **only an invite creates a user**. The owner (`OWNER_USER_ID`) is inserted by migration `0018_auth_identity` on every database (never lazily), role `admin`, no credentials until claimed — beyond being the first admin it is not special. Every other user comes from `inviteUser` (`controllers/users.ts`, admin-only): it inserts an unclaimed row (username + role, no password) with its `invites` row (sha256 of the code, 72 h, single use, at most one unclaimed per user), and the person chooses their own password by claiming it at `/ui/access/invite` (`claimInvite` only `update`s that row — nothing creates a user at claim time; the admin never learns the password). `reissueInvite` replaces an invite, and for a claimed user is an admin-driven reset (password cleared; every session, token, stdio sign-in and approved sign-in request ended in the same batch); `disableUser` ends the same credentials, approved sign-in requests included, in the batch that disables (users are disabled, never deleted; `enableUser` revives nothing). **User management is session-only and admin-only** — browser pages under `/ui/access/users` (a member gets the not-found reply) and the trusted terminal's `users` command; never an MCP tool, never an `/api` route, never reachable with a bearer token. Invite, reissue, disable, enable, set-role and the sign-in cap re-ask the admin's password (the terminal has none), and re-read the admin's browser session on every attempt (the `Principal` carries `sessionId`; the batch checks its version), so a retry after that session was revoked is refused. **The instance always keeps one active admin** (`guardAdminChange`; nobody disables or demotes themself; the admins left standing are checked in the same batch so concurrent changes conflict and retry; every flow that issues a way in — a token, an approved or redeemed sign-in, an invite, a login — writes the user's `credentials_changed_at`, so a revocation that read their credentials earlier conflicts with it in either order). `settings.max_sign_in_duration` (`24h|7d|30d`, default `30d`) caps what `approveGrant` grants and what `redeemGrant` mints (an approval made before the cap fell is clamped at redemption) — a sign-in already minted keeps its expiry. The invite code is a short-lived bearer secret: never logged (the logger redacts the `code` query parameter), the claim page answers `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin`. `/ui/setup` + the setup code, or the terminal's `setup`/`auth setup` (`claimOwnerLocally`: no code, no session, any outstanding code spent in the same batch — reachable only by someone who can open the database with its key), **claims** it (an `update`; no flow inserts a user). `auth reset-password` (`resetPassword`) updates the hash, deletes that user's sessions, revokes their live access tokens and expires their approved sign-in requests in one batch (`logic/auth/revoke.ts`'s `endedCredentials` is the one rule for every revocation). Passwords are argon2id; session tokens and setup codes are stored only as sha256 and never persisted in plaintext — the token is never logged, and the setup code is printed exactly once, to stderr, when issued (the owner needs it to claim the instance) and nowhere else; a session expires 24 hours after it was last seen and never later than 30 days after login (`SESSION_IDLE_TTL_MS`, `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MAX_MS`); the `fintrack_session` cookie is `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` (+`Secure` under an https `PUBLIC_URL`); cookie-authenticated unsafe requests are Origin-checked, and with auth disabled only loopback `Host`/`Origin` requests are answered (DNS-rebinding guard). **Access tokens (ADR-033 Phase 2):** `ftk_` + 32 random bytes (`TOKEN_PREFIX`), stored only as sha256 + a display prefix in `access_tokens` (migration `0019_access_tokens`, not data-rewriting), plaintext shown once at creation and never logged; expiry is 30/90/365 days — there is no "never" for new tokens (ADR-034 §6; a legacy null `expires_at` row keeps working until revoked and lists as "No expiry (legacy)"); creating one re-asks the login password (step-up, so a script in a dashboard's origin cannot mint itself a token); scopes `fintrack:read`/`fintrack:write` (write implies read, `logic/auth/scope.ts`'s `hasScope`). On `/api` and `/mcp` an `Authorization` header is authoritative — it must be a valid `Bearer ftk_…`, the cookie is then never consulted (a bad bearer never falls back to a session) and there is no CSRF check; `/ui` stays session-only and token management is session-only (a token can never mint or widen another), and with auth disabled the header is ignored. Every `RouteDefinition` declares a `scope` (GET/HEAD → read, else write) and every MCP tool declares `annotations.readOnlyHint` (the single source of its scope; `guardToolScopes` refuses a tool without it); a `Principal` carries `scopes` and `via` (`session|token|owner|stdio`), the session and the trusted owner hold every scope. 401/403 `WWW-Authenticate` challenges are built in one place (`logic/auth/bearer.ts`'s `bearerChallenge`) and point at the Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/mcp]`. A migration listed in `diplomat/db/migrations.ts`'s `DATA_REWRITING_MIGRATIONS` first copies the database to `<DB_PATH>.pre-<migration>.bak`. **Stdio sign-ins (ADR-034)** are `access_tokens` rows with `kind: stdio` (`client_name`, `profile`, always an `expires_at`; expiry is absolute from approval, never slid), minted by `redeemGrant` from an approved `client_grants` row — a device-style grant: the asking process holds the plaintext device code (only its sha256 is stored), the link carries the **user code only** (never a secret in a URL or tool result), `approveGrant` is session-only, re-asks the password (step-up) and binds the approving user, redemption is single-use, a pending grant lives 10 minutes. A stdio token authenticates through the same `authenticateToken` as a PAT but is accepted only on the stdio channel (`PrincipalVia.stdio`), and is re-validated on every tool call, resource read and prompt get (`StdioSession`, behind the `PrincipalGate` of `diplomat/mcp/gate.ts`, which grants the WHOLE `Principal` on every transport; every sign-in decision — stdio and `login` alike — is `logic/auth/sign-in-flow.ts`'s `nextStep`, executed by `src/composition/sign-in/interpreter.ts`, which `src/composition/sign-in/wiring.ts`'s `createSignInFor` builds and the flows in `src/composition/` inject). The sign-in link names only `PUBLIC_URL` or the sidecar this process bound — never the configured `HOST:PORT` (another process there may have opened a different database); with neither, the session serves `/ui/connect` itself from a temporary `localhost` server on this database, closed once the request is redeemed, denied or expired and at shutdown. `pruneExpiredGrants` also drops redeemed grants superseded per (user, profile, client). "This session only" is kept in memory and never written to the keychain (account `signin:<profile>:<dbId>`). `bootstrap` refuses a database newer than the build (`checkDatabaseNotAhead`, returning a `DatabaseAhead` error) before anything is copied, migrated or seeded.
- SQL queries: always use Drizzle's parameterized API or the `sql` template tag — never interpolate user input into query strings.

## Documentation map (read before generating)

**Taxonomy (keep each doc in its lane).** Canonical concept docs (`docs/diplomatic-architecture.md`, `docs/functional-core-imperative-shell.md`) are **agnostic** — concepts and the obligations to satisfy them, with **no** project nouns, identifiers, library names, ADR references, or status/phase tracking. Project specifics (schema, concrete types, structures), the ADR index, and current-state/next-steps live in `docs/architecture.md`, kept **current-only** (prune replaced concepts — no ghosts). Operational rules live in `docs/code-style.md`/`docs/code-quality.md`. A canonical doc that names a project entity, identifier, ADR, or phase is a taxonomy violation — move it to `docs/architecture.md`. **Check this on any docs change (self-review).**

- `docs/architecture.md` — the system **as built**: relational schema, invariants, layer rules. The source of truth when generating code; if your change alters it, update it in the same change.
- `docs/diplomatic-architecture.md`: The Diplomatic Architecture core concepts.
- `docs/functional-core-imperative-shell.md` — Functional Core / Imperative Shell: what the domain declares as effects (as data) and what the shell executes. Mandatory alongside the Diplomatic Architecture doc for write-flow changes; see `docs/architecture.md` for this project's concrete types and current state.
- `docs/code-style.md` — code style with do/don't examples (safeTry controllers, remeda pipelines, zod-only types). Generated code MUST match these patterns.
- `docs/code-quality.md` — quality principles: constants over literals, naming, single responsibility, no magic values. Read before generating any code.
- `docs/PLAN.md` — roadmap/vision; updated at phase boundaries, may lag the as-built state.
- `docs/adr/` — decisions with rationale; never contradict an accepted ADR without writing a new one.
- `docs/mcp-tools.md` — MCP tool contract. `docs/mcp-clients.md` — client connection guide.

## Process

- Architecture decisions get an ADR in `docs/adr/` (use the `engineering:architecture` skill if available; otherwise follow the ADR template in `docs/adr/` and include rationale + decision + consequences).
- Docs are updated in the same change that alters behavior — `docs/architecture.md` for structural changes, `docs/mcp-tools.md` for tool changes.
- New MCP tools must be documented in `docs/mcp-tools.md` with schema, error codes, and an example.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`. Use `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer for incompatible changes.

## Git workflow (branch + PR only)

`main` is **protected — never commit or push directly to it.** All changes land via pull request:

1. Branch off the latest `main`: `git checkout main && git pull && git checkout -b type/short-description` (branch name uses the Conventional Commit type, e.g. `refactor/classification-history`, `docs/contributing-workflow`).
2. Commit on the branch (Conventional Commits), `git push -u origin <branch>`.
3. Open a PR targeting `main`: `gh pr create --base main --fill` (or with an explicit `--title`/`--body`). CI must pass and the PR must be reviewed before merge.
4. After merge, the feature branch is deleted; pull `main` before starting the next branch.

If work was accidentally committed to local `main`, move it before pushing: `git branch <feature>` then `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && git checkout <feature>`, and continue on `<feature>`.

## Pull request comments

When working on a PR — addressing review feedback, pushing fixes, or responding to comments — always reply to every open review comment on that PR after the work is done. Use `gh api graphql` with `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply` to post replies (the REST replies endpoint is unreliable). Each reply should reference the commit SHA that resolves it so the thread is traceable.

Do this automatically without waiting to be asked.

## Tech debt

When a known trade-off is deliberately deferred during a PR or feature — a performance optimization, a correctness edge case, a refactor — create a **GitHub Issue** to track it. Do not create local markdown files for this purpose.

The issue body should include:
- What the current code does and why it's suboptimal
- The improved approach (with code/query snippet if applicable)
- Why it was deferred
- When it should be tackled (trigger condition or milestone)
- Rough effort estimate

After creating the issue, reference it in the PR description or review thread so the connection is traceable.
